tasks.short: Write the job on a paper work order, check it and sign the release of the device, retype it into the maintenance system, track required updates per device, and set the next maintenance date.

steps.what: Medical equipment technician writes the maintenance or repair job on a paper work order
Medical equipment technician checks the record and signs the release of the equipment for use
Medical equipment technician retypes the work order into the maintenance system
Medical equipment technician tracks required updates and safety notices per device in a spreadsheet
Medical equipment technician sets the next maintenance date by hand

tasks.design: The technician completes a mobile work order in the maintenance system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) at the device: the barcode picks the device, fault and cause come from pick lists, parts are scanned and times taken from start and stop taps. After the technician checks and signs the release, the record is stored on the device's history without retyping, and the next date follows from the maintenance plan. Manufacturer safety notices and software updates are linked to device types, so the system lists affected devices instead of a spreadsheet.
tasks.previous_blocker: Work orders were written on paper and retyped; updates were tracked in a spreadsheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Maintenance systems run mobile work orders with barcodes and device histories.
tasks.still_hard: External service reports still arrive on paper.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding a repaired pump is safe to use on a patient again.
tasks.altitude: The technician checks records instead of writing them twice.

reach.learn: Whether every device has a current release.

evidence.claim: Ultimo EAM has a medical-device module and barcode fault reporting for hospital technicians.
Altitude Infra reported about 8 hours per technician per week saved on work-order mail, entry and reports with Praxedo; vendor case, period not stated.
The Dutch hospital medical technology covenant asks for maintenance procedures and formal release after every job.
Work orders with time stamps can observe technicians and need works council consent first.

assumptions: Boundary: from the job done to the next date set; buying parts is outside.
Input contract: devices barcoded and plans loaded; fallback is paper.
The technician checks and signs every release.
Works council consent comes before time taps are used.
research_questions: Are affected devices found sooner after a safety notice?

incremental.description: Medical equipment technician links new safety notices to device types.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many external paper reports; high: in-house work on barcoded devices.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Inspect equipment and its surroundings for hazards, run electrical safety tests, copy readings and compare them with limits, check how staff use equipment, and record findings.

steps.what: Medical equipment technician examines medical equipment and the facility's structural environment for hazards
Medical equipment technician performs electrical safety tests with an analyser
Medical equipment technician copies readings onto the test form and compares them with safety limits
Medical equipment technician checks for proper use of equipment by staff on the ward
Medical equipment technician records findings and hazard reports on paper

tasks.design: The safety analyser exports its test results to the device record in the maintenance system ({OPS_SYSTEM}), which compares each reading with the limit for that device class and marks failures, so readings are not copied and compared by hand. Findings and hazard reports go into a form on the device or location record. Inspecting, testing and checking how staff use equipment stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readings were copied from the analyser onto paper forms and findings filed on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Safety analysers export results; maintenance systems hold limits per device class.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing a frayed cable taped up behind a bed.

reach.task: Keep equipment safe on the ward
reach.learn: Whether findings reach the ward sooner.

evidence.claim: Electrical safety analysers can export test results to maintenance systems.
The Dutch hospital medical technology covenant asks for maintenance procedures and formal release after every job.

assumptions: Boundary: from the inspection due to findings recorded; repairs are outside.
Input contract: analyser linked to the system; fallback is the paper form.
Inspection and testing do not change.
Ward staff's time does not change.
s5 is part of keeping maintenance and repair records, which sibling task 49-9062.00:3064 covers; its saving is counted there, so s5 keeps its full time here.
research_questions: Do transcription errors on test forms disappear?

incremental.description: Medical equipment technician keeps limits per device class current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older analysers; high: analysers with export.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review the work assignment and device history, find the right manual or schematic, plan the repair, and carry out the work following prescribed procedures.

steps.what: Medical equipment technician reviews the work assignment and the device history
Medical equipment technician finds the right technical manual, schematic drawings or wiring diagrams
Medical equipment technician plans work assignments from the schematics and instructions
Medical equipment technician carries out the work following prescribed regulations

tasks.design: The work order in the maintenance system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) opens with the device history, and the service manual, schematics and current service bulletins are linked to the device type, so the technician does not search binders and vendor portals. Planning and carrying out the work stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manuals sat in binders and vendor portals and histories in separate files.
tasks.enabler_now: Maintenance systems link documents to device types.
tasks.human_edge: Reading a wiring diagram for a device the vendor no longer supports.

evidence.claim: Ultimo EAM keeps preventive plans and repair history per asset.

assumptions: Boundary: from the work assignment to the work done; release is outside.
Input contract: documents linked per device type; fallback is binders.
Planning and the work itself do not change.
Vendors allow manuals to be stored.
research_questions: Is time spent finding documents shorter?

incremental.description: Medical equipment technician links new manuals and bulletins to device types.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few device types; high: many device types and bulletins.

tasks.short: Attend manufacturer training sessions, study technical manuals and bulletins, and keep the record of training and device authorisations.

steps.what: Medical equipment technician attends training sessions provided by equipment manufacturers
Medical equipment technician studies technical manuals to maintain current knowledge
Medical equipment technician records training and device authorisations in a spreadsheet

tasks.design: Training certificates are uploaded to the technician's record in the learning system ({LMS}), which is linked to device types in the maintenance system, so work orders go only to technicians trained on that device and expiring authorisations are listed. Attending training and studying manuals stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Training and authorisations were kept in a spreadsheet nobody checked at assignment.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning systems hold certificates; maintenance systems can check skills at assignment.
tasks.still_hard: Vendor certificates come in many formats.
tasks.human_edge: Learning a new device well enough to trust a repair on it.

reach.learn: Whether jobs go to trained technicians.

evidence.claim: Maintenance systems can store training per device type and limit work orders to trained technicians.
AI that allocates work by behaviour or traits is high-risk; rule-based checks on training are outside it.

assumptions: Boundary: from the new device to training recorded; training budgets are outside.
Input contract: certificates uploaded after each course; fallback is the spreadsheet.
Training and study time do not change.
research_questions: Do jobs on devices without trained staff fall?

incremental.description: Medical equipment technician uploads certificates after each course.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few courses; high: many device types and expiring authorisations.
